title: Chest pressure in a 41-year-old line cook
intended_learner: Medical students and first-year emergency medicine residents
unknown_response: I'm not sure. I can't really tell you anything about that.
prebrief: You are the emergency medicine resident. Rafael Quintero, 41, walked in with chest pressure that started about two hours ago. Triage has taken vital signs. Take a focused history, request the examination and tests you need, and decide on a disposition. You have about eight minutes.

profile.name: Rafael Quintero
profile.background: Line cook at a busy restaurant, works double shifts, lives with his partner and young daughter.
profile.personality: Proud, guarded, minimises problems; warms up when treated with respect.
profile.speech_style: Short, plain sentences. Deflects with 'I'm fine'.

faculty_truth.diagnosis: Cocaine-associated chest pain with possible non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
teaching_points: Ask every chest pain patient about stimulant use, and ask again when the evidence does not fit the answer.
A guarded patient is more likely to disclose after a non-judging explanation of why the question matters for treatment.
A first troponin above the reference needs a repeat and observation, not discharge.

facts.statement: Central chest pressure that began about two hours before arrival
facts.patient_answer: I've got this pressure in the middle of my chest. It started a couple of hours ago and it scared me enough to come in.

facts.statement: Onset at rest, around 6 am, while getting ready for a shift; woke feeling unwell
facts.patient_answer: It came on around six this morning. I wasn't doing anything, just getting ready for work.

facts.statement: Pressure-like, 'a weight on the chest', not sharp or tearing
facts.patient_answer: It's like a weight sitting on my chest. Pressure. It's not sharp.

facts.statement: Pain was 7/10 at its worst, 4/10 on arrival
facts.patient_answer: It was about a seven at its worst. Maybe a four right now.

facts.statement: Radiates to the left shoulder and left side of the jaw
facts.patient_answer: Yeah, it goes into my left shoulder, and my jaw aches on that side.

facts.statement: Constant for roughly two hours, easing slightly since arrival
facts.patient_answer: It's been there the whole time, about two hours. It's eased off a little since I got here.

facts.statement: Not changed by breathing, position or pressing on the chest; nothing taken for it
facts.patient_answer: Nothing really changes it. Breathing, moving, pressing on it, it's all the same. I didn't take anything.

facts.statement: Sweating, palpitations and nausea with the pain; no vomiting, no shortness of breath at rest
facts.patient_answer: I was sweating a lot, my heart was pounding, and I felt sick to my stomach. I didn't throw up. My breathing is okay.

facts.statement: One similar, milder episode about eight months ago that settled within an hour
facts.patient_answer: Something like this happened once before, maybe eight months back. It was milder and went away in an hour.

facts.statement: Denies fever, cough, leg swelling, calf pain, recent travel or immobilisation, syncope
facts.patient_answer: No fever, no cough. My legs are fine, no swelling. I haven't travelled anywhere and I didn't pass out.

facts.statement: Told two years ago that his blood pressure was borderline high; never treated or followed up
facts.patient_answer: A doctor told me a couple of years ago my blood pressure was borderline. I never went back about it.

facts.statement: No known diabetes, high cholesterol (never tested), heart disease or prior surgery
facts.patient_answer: No diabetes that I know of. I've never had my cholesterol checked. No heart problems before, no surgeries.

facts.statement: No regular prescription medicines; occasional ibuprofen for back ache; energy drinks most shifts
facts.patient_answer: I'm not on any regular medicines. Ibuprofen now and then for my back. I do drink a couple of energy drinks most shifts.

facts.statement: No known drug allergies
facts.patient_answer: No allergies that I know of.

facts.statement: Father had a heart attack at age 52 and died at 60; mother has type 2 diabetes
facts.patient_answer: My dad had a heart attack at fifty-two. He died at sixty. My mom has diabetes.

facts.statement: Smokes about half a pack of cigarettes a day for 20 years (about 10 pack-years)
facts.patient_answer: About half a pack a day. I started when I was around twenty.

facts.statement: Drinks three or four beers after a shift, three nights a week
facts.patient_answer: A few beers after a shift. Three, four, maybe three nights a week.

facts.statement: Line cook working double shifts; behind on rent; sleeps about five hours a night
facts.patient_answer: I'm a line cook. I've been pulling doubles because I'm behind on rent, so I sleep maybe five hours.

facts.statement: Lives with his partner and their seven-year-old daughter
facts.patient_answer: I live with my partner and our daughter. She's seven.

facts.statement: Used intranasal cocaine at about 1 am, roughly five hours before the pain began; uses it about twice a month to get through double shifts
facts.patient_answer: Okay. Yes. I did a couple of lines of coke around one this morning, to get through a double. I do it maybe twice a month. I didn't want it on my record, and I didn't want my partner finding out.
facts.cover_answer: No. I don't do drugs. Just the energy drinks.

facts.statement: Afraid of losing his job and of his daughter seeing him ill; his father died of heart disease
facts.patient_answer: Honestly, I'm scared. My dad died of this. And if I can't work, we lose the apartment. I keep thinking about my daughter.
facts.cover_answer: I'm fine. I just want to get this checked and get back to work.

facts.statement: Heart rate 112 beats/min
facts.label: Heart rate

facts.statement: Blood pressure 168/102 mmHg
facts.label: Blood pressure

facts.statement: Respiratory rate 20/min, SpO2 98% on room air, temperature 37.4 C
Anxious, diaphoretic, restless; pupils 6 mm and reactive
Regular tachycardia, no murmur, rub or gallop; chest wall not tender
Lungs clear bilaterally; no leg oedema, calves soft
ECG: sinus tachycardia 110/min, 1 mm ST depression in V4-V6, no ST elevation
High-sensitivity troponin 31 ng/L at presentation (this laboratory's reference: below 14 ng/L)
facts.label: Troponin

facts.statement: Urine drug screen: cocaine metabolite detected
facts.label: Cocaine metabolite

artifacts.title: Triage note
artifacts.content: 41-year-old man, walked in. Central chest pressure for about 2 hours, sweaty and restless at triage. Says he has 'no medical problems'. Pain 4/10 now. ESI 2. ECG requested per chest pain pathway (not yet reviewed).

artifacts.title: 12-lead ECG (text description)
artifacts.content: Rate 110/min, sinus rhythm. Normal axis. PR 150 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 450 ms. ST depression of about 1 mm in V4, V5 and V6. No ST elevation. No pathological Q waves. No previous ECG on file for comparison.
artifacts.interpretation: Sinus tachycardia with lateral ST depression: ischaemia cannot be excluded. Together with the raised troponin this needs serial ECGs and troponins.

artifacts.title: Blood results (first set)
artifacts.interpretation: Troponin above this laboratory's reference at presentation; the troponin reference is assay-specific and authored for this synthetic case. A repeat is needed to see the trend.

artifacts.title: Urine drug screen
artifacts.interpretation: Screening immunoassay consistent with recent cocaine exposure. A screen does not time the exposure or prove the cause of the chest pain.

artifacts.title: Previous emergency visit (8 months ago)
artifacts.content: Seen 8 months ago with palpitations and chest tightness that settled within an hour. Heart rate 124 on arrival. ECG: sinus tachycardia only. Patient reported using 'something from a coworker to stay awake'. Left before a drug screen was collected. Advised to follow up for blood pressure 150/96; no follow-up recorded.
artifacts.interpretation: A documented earlier stimulant-related episode and an untreated raised blood pressure.

objectives.criterion: Characterises the chest pain: onset, character, radiation and associated symptoms
objectives.evidence_rule: met when all four are elicited; partly when some are
objectives.feedback_met: You built a clear picture of the pain before moving on.
objectives.feedback_missed: Work through onset, character, radiation and associated symptoms for any chest pain.

objectives.criterion: Elicits cardiac risk factors: smoking, blood pressure and family history
objectives.evidence_rule: met when all three are elicited
objectives.feedback_missed: Ask about smoking, blood pressure, diabetes, cholesterol and heart disease in close relatives.

objectives.criterion: Uncovers recent stimulant use despite the patient's initial denial
objectives.evidence_rule: met when the patient discloses cocaine use; partly when the learner asks about drugs but accepts the denial
objectives.feedback_met: You noticed that the story and the evidence did not match, and raised it in a way that let him answer honestly.
objectives.feedback_missed: He denied drug use, but the previous visit note and the urine screen say otherwise. Request them, then raise what you found without judgement and explain why it changes treatment.

objectives.criterion: Requests an ECG and a troponin
objectives.feedback_missed: Chest pressure with sweating needs an ECG straight away and a troponin.

objectives.criterion: Responds to the patient's fear and uses non-judging language on sensitive topics
objectives.evidence_rule: empathic or normalising statements; strongest evidence is the patient sharing what he is afraid of
objectives.feedback_missed: He says 'I'm fine' but he is frightened. Name it, and tell him sensitive questions are routine and confidential.

objectives.criterion: Runs a structured interview: introduction, open question first, summary, clear close
objectives.evidence_rule: three of: introduction, early open question, summary, closing

objectives.criterion: Recognises that this patient needs observation and repeat testing rather than discharge
objectives.evidence_rule: disposition is admit, with a summary that names the ECG change or the raised troponin
objectives.feedback_missed: ST depression and a raised first troponin mean he should stay for serial testing.
